report.audience: entertainment industry analyst or film music historian

brief.title: Nine Decades of Oscar-Winning Scores: A Historical Trend Analysis (1934–2026)
brief.one_liner: A comprehensive analysis of every Academy Award Best Original Score winner, exploring composer dominance, stylistic evolution, and historical patterns across 93 ceremonies.
brief.goal: The reader should gain a clear understanding of which composers have shaped the Oscar landscape, how winning score styles have evolved over time, and what recurring patterns or notable anomalies define the history of the Best Original Score category.

required_sections.title: Dataset Overview & Historical Context
required_sections.objective: Introduce the scope of the dataset (93 ceremonies, 1934–2026), summarize key statistics (total unique composers, total unique films), and provide brief historical context for the Academy Award for Best Original Score.

required_sections.title: Most Awarded Composers
required_sections.objective: Identify and rank composers by number of wins. Highlight repeat winners, discuss the most dominant figures in Oscar scoring history, and note any ties or close competitions.

required_sections.title: Temporal Patterns & Decade-by-Decade Breakdown
required_sections.objective: Analyze how wins distribute across decades. Identify decades with the most repeat winners versus the most diverse winner pools. Highlight any notable streaks, gaps, or clustering of wins.

required_sections.title: Era-Based Analysis of Winning Scores
required_sections.objective: Using approximate era boundaries (e.g., Golden Age 1934–1960s, Silver Age 1960s–1980s, Modern 1980s–2000s, Contemporary 2000s–2026), characterize each era's defining composers and any observable shifts in the types of films that win.

required_sections.title: Notable Milestones & Records
required_sections.objective: Highlight landmark moments: first-time winners, youngest/oldest implied winners, longest gaps between wins for a single composer, and the most recent winner (Ludwig Göransson for Sinners, 2026).

required_sections.title: Key Takeaways & Forward-Looking Observations
required_sections.objective: Synthesize findings into 3–5 key takeaways about the evolution of Oscar-winning scores and offer observations about emerging trends heading into the late 2020s.

kpis.name: Total Unique Composers
kpis.description: Count of distinct composers who have won the Best Original Score Oscar across all 93 ceremonies.

kpis.name: Maximum Wins by a Single Composer
kpis.description: The highest number of Best Original Score wins achieved by any individual composer.

kpis.name: Repeat Winner Rate
kpis.description: Percentage of ceremonies won by a composer who had already won at least once before.

kpis.name: Decade with Most Unique Winners
kpis.description: The decade (e.g., 1990s) that featured the greatest number of distinct winning composers.
